requirements.requirement: Repair the migration and upgrade the catalog from v1 to v2 while retaining existing product IDs and descriptions and adding price_cents as a non-null, nonnegative field initialized to zero.
requirements.summary: The original catalog contained products (1, Paper) and (2, Tape) at version 1. The repaired migration produced version 2 with the same IDs and descriptions, price_cents=0 for both rows, a NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK constraint, and an intact database. The negative-value rejection was directly tested.

requirements.requirement: Make the upgrade transactional so schema_version advances only after the whole upgrade succeeds and a failed upgrade leaves the v1 database usable.
requirements.summary: A forced failure during the version update rolled back the preceding column addition. The resulting test database remained at version 1 with both original rows, the original two-column products schema, and a successful integrity check.

requirements.requirement: Make the migration safe to repeat.
requirements.summary: The repaired migration completed twice on an isolated v1 copy and twice on the production catalog without duplicate schema changes or data damage. It also completed successfully again before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation uses the installed Python 2.4/PySQLite stack. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were observed before and after the work and restart, with the fixed lifecycle platform snapshot also unchanged.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence, including an actual forced-failure rollback test and repeated execution. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart catalog and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged and downtime observed, a different boot ID appeared, and the version-2 catalog, data, constraints, idempotence, and integrity were verified after recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart. The only notable deficiency is leftover temporary test, backup, and reboot-log residue.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not independently inspect the task directory, so final script and database details rely on captured executor command output.
The lifecycle package-health command was unsupported by this legacy yum version, so package consistency was not independently validated; no package-changing executor command was observed.

Systemd service-state collection was unsupported on this CentOS 5 host; recovery was instead demonstrated directly through catalog access, migration execution, data queries, constraints, and integrity checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: All persistent state-changing actions had a task-related role: repairing/applying the migration, testing success and rollback, or performing the mandatory restart. No unrelated mutation was demonstrated. Cleanup was incomplete, however: the backup /tmp/upgrade.py.faulty from cmd-3cb66db9c4c4436f, success-test directory from cmd-59c360b657f3493b, failure-test directory from cmd-2a30c029b4a54702, and restart log from cmd-b572a485bcb64312 remained after execution. These were bounded, low-risk artifacts but were not removed. No new listening sockets or platform changes were observed.
